Breaking an alliance or attacking an ally is a betrayal: traitor mark and halved defence for 30 s, plus an automatic embargo. Any attacked country stops trading with its aggressor for 5 minutes.

air.desc: Airfields and interceptors, bombers (strikes on buildings), fighters, reconnaissance.

radar.desc: Early warning and interceptor guidance within 60 tiles; reveal the fog.

rampart.name: Rampart
rampart.desc: Defence posts twice as effective for 30 s.

sabotage.name: Sabotage
sabotage.desc: Destroys the enemy train or merchant ship nearest the target point.

propaganda.name: Propaganda
propaganda.desc: +50% loyalty for 60 s, no secession possible.

city.name: City
city.desc: +60,000 maximum troops per level once built. Railway station.

port.name: Port
port.desc: Built on the coast. Sends merchant ships to foreign ports: both ports earn the cargo, worth more on long routes. Acts as a station. Radius of action of 60 tiles (+10 per level): warships are built inside it. A damaged warship docks here to be repaired.

factory.name: Factory
factory.desc: Lays railways to stations within 110 tiles and runs trains.

defensePost.name: Defence post
defensePost.desc: Within 30 tiles: attacker losses ×5, speed ×3. Destroyed when captured.

silo.name: Missile silo
silo.desc: Launches A-bombs, H-bombs and MIRVs. Each upgrade adds a tube.

sam.name: SAM battery
sam.desc: Intercepts bombs and warheads with trajectory prediction. Range 49 → 105 tiles by level.

radar.name: Radar tower
radar.desc: 60-tile coverage (+20 per level): early warning of incoming aircraft and transports, guides interceptors up to 90 tiles from your airfields; reveals the fog.

airfield.name: Airfield
airfield.desc: Launches fighters, bombers and reconnaissance (4 in flight per level). One alert interceptor per level scrambles at detected bombers and reconnaissance: 50 tiles, 90 under your radars.

lab.name: Research centre
lab.desc: Produces 1.5 research points per second per level once built; without a centre, research crawls at 0.5 point/s. Unlimited levels. Changes hands when captured.

warship.name: Warship
warship.desc: Placed on water, within the radius of action of one of your ports. Firing range 90 tiles; targets transports first, then warships, and captures merchants. Gains veterancy and patrols around its anchor point.

fighter.name: Fighter
fighter.desc: Patrols for 60 s within 90 tiles of an airfield: shoots down bombers, fighters, reconnaissance and invading transports within 30 tiles. Escorts your raids, covers a front or a coast.

bomber.name: Bomber
bomber.desc: Hits the enemy building nearest the target (range 300): −1 level, destroyed at level 1; silos and SAMs lose their loaded missiles. Two levels under your reconnaissance. Shot down by SAMs and fighters.

recon.name: Reconnaissance
recon.desc: 40 s over a 40-tile zone (range 400): your attacks there lose 25% fewer troops, your bombers hit two levels, and hovering there reveals treasury, loaded tubes and ready missiles.

campaign.title: Campaign: The Cartographers
campaign.intro: Six missions that teach you the game: drawing, holding and defending your lines. Each mission awards up to three stars: success, speed and bonus objective.
campaign.failed: We lost our lands. Let's try again.

m1.title: First Lines
m1.outro: Fine first lines. The nations have noticed your ink.
m1.brief: Two great lakes divide this region. Three small nations are settling here, surrounded by tribes that guard their gold. You start with a capital and a few thousand men. I will guide you step by step: expand, build a city, subdue the tribes, and become a regional power by controlling fifteen percent of the land.
m1.tip1: A click on unclaimed land sends part of your troops there, as set by the attack ratio at the bottom left. Several small clicks beat a single large one.
m1.tip2: Cities raise your troop ceiling. Your starting treasury pays for the first one; each new city costs twice as much as the previous one.
m1.bonusLevels: Own 2 cities (a level-2 city counts as two)

m2.title: Hold the Line
m2.outro: Your lines held. The attackers broke against your ramparts.
m2.brief: Europe is a powder keg. Thirty nations fight over every valley, and the difficulty is set to hard. You will not win this war; the task is not to lose it. Hold out for twenty minutes without being wiped off the map.
m2.tip1: Mountains, hills and forests cost the attacker more: lean on them.
m2.tip2: A defence post multiplies the attacker's losses by five within thirty tiles.

m3.title: The Island
m3.brief: An archipelago of hundreds of islands: here, every conquest goes through the sea. A dozen nations share the coasts, and their warships sink careless transports. Land on another island, then eliminate at least one rival nation; tribes don't count.
m3.tip1: Aim at a coast across the water and press B: a transport sails from your nearest shore. At most three can be at sea at the same time.
m3.tip2: A port lets you fit out warships (key 7) to escort your landings. Storms slow every ship down.

m4.title: Rails and Riches
m4.outro: Your iron lines became lines of credit.
m4.brief: Pangaea joins all land into a single continent: trade routes here are long and lucrative. Your goal is not conquest but fortune: earn one and a half million gold through sea trade and trains, and research railways in your first research centre.
m4.tip1: A factory automatically links your nearby cities, ports and factories by rail. Every train stop pays gold.
m4.tip2: Ports send merchant ships to foreign ports; an embargo cuts that trade. Press C to show the trade routes.

m5.title: Artificial Sun
m5.bonus: Intercept a missile with a SAM
m5.outro: The world saw your sun. It will not forget it.
m5.brief: The Mediterranean, cradle of empires. Some borders are only drawn in fire. Build a research centre, complete the nuclear programme, then launch a hydrogen bomb. Beware, enemy SAM batteries can intercept it.
m5.tip1: A silo costs one million and the hydrogen bomb five, and both must be researched first. The more research centres you have, the faster the research.
m5.tip2: Aim far from any SAM battery: the missile can be intercepted in flight.

m6.title: One Minute to Midnight
m6.outro: You stopped the clock. The atlas now bears your name.
m6.brief: The whole world, and the doomsday clock ticking: every bomb, every fallen country, every betrayal brings it closer to midnight. Four milestones change the rules on the way, and at midnight everything stops. Reach forty percent of the world before then.
m6.tip1: The dial under the top bar shows the time, the next milestone and its effect. From "Survival of the strongest", below the land threshold your troops melt away.
m6.tip2: Tribes and unclaimed land are your first targets; keep the big wars for later.

subtitle.capitalLost: War horn: your capital has fallen

guide.spawn: Choose where to place your capital: click on unclaimed land, ideally away from other nations. The match starts as soon as you have placed it.

m1.camera: Drag the map to move around, and zoom with the mouse wheel or a trackpad pinch. Press H to come back to your territory.
m1.expand: Expand: click on unclaimed land along your border. Your troops advance on their own while they have the strength.
m1.ratio: At the bottom left, the attack ratio sets the share of your troops sent with each click. Change it with T and Y, or Shift and the mouse wheel: a low ratio keeps troops back for defence.
m1.city: Your population soon reaches its ceiling. Build a city: press 1 then click your territory, or right click, Build, City.
m1.tribes: Tribes, in grey, guard a treasury. Attack one: each piece of land you take yields a share of its gold.
m1.capital: The star on your territory marks your capital. If it falls, your country is disorganised for a minute and you will have to choose a new one: keep it away from the front.
m1.goal: Keep going until you hold fifteen percent of the land. A second city earns the bonus star.

m2.spawn: Place your capital. Rugged terrain, such as the Alps or the Carpathians, will be easier to defend.
m2.expand: Take unclaimed land quickly, before neighbouring nations surround you.
m2.defense: Build a defence post (key 4) near your most exposed border.
m2.threats: When a neighbour masses a much bigger army on your border, a “threatened border” alert appears and the journal records it. Reinforce that front, or make that neighbour an ally.
m2.alliance: Propose an alliance to a neighbour: right click its territory, or use the Diplomacy window in the left rail. Offers you receive appear at the bottom right: K to accept, L to refuse.
m2.troops: Let your army regrow before attacking again: reach half of your troop ceiling.
m2.hold: Hold out until the countdown ends. Reinforce the fronts that give way and renew your alliances.

m3.island: Start by taking your whole island.
m3.port: Build a port (key 2) on your coast: it brings sea trade and lets you fit out warships.
m3.landing: The weakest nation is marked on the map. Aim at its coast and press B, or right click then Land troops: a transport sails from your nearest shore with the ratio's share of your troops.
m3.boats: At most three transports can be at sea at once. They are listed in the panel at the bottom left: the return arrow recalls one, at the cost of a quarter of its troops. Storms slow every ship down.
m3.warship: Enemy warships sink transports. Fit out your own: press 7, then click the sea near your port. It escorts your landings and attacks enemy ships.
m3.finish: Keep going until it is eliminated. Send reinforcements by sea if the attack runs out of steam.

m4.expand: Expand to make room: railways need distance between stations.
m4.cities: Build two cities: they will be your first stations.
m4.factory: Build a factory (key 3) between your cities. The tracks are laid automatically.
m4.port: Build a port to add sea trade to your income.
m4.routes: Trains and merchant ships pay at every stop. Press C to show or hide the trade routes; the Trade window, in the left rail, details your earnings per partner.
m4.lab: Build a research centre (key J): it produces research points, even while nothing is being studied.
m4.research: Open the Technologies window and click Railways: its prerequisite is queued ahead of it. Add more technologies: they will be studied in order.
m4.windows: Windows move by their title bar and resize from their corner; Escape closes the one in front. They stay where you put them.
m4.wait: Your network is running. Add factories and stations to multiply stops, and avoid wars that cut the lines.

m5.expand: Expand to build up your economy.
m5.lab: Build a research centre (key J): it produces the research points.
m5.research: Open the Technologies window and click Nuclear programme: its prerequisites are queued ahead of it. A second research centre would speed up the research.
m5.city: Build two cities to raise population and income.
m5.silo: Once the nuclear programme is researched, build a missile silo (key 5).
m5.hbomb: Now put the thermonuclear bomb under study. Think about SAM batteries too (key 6, once surface-to-air missiles are researched): they shoot down enemy missiles.
m5.launch: Press 9 then click an enemy target. A possible target is marked on the map.

m6.expand: Expand as fast as you can.
m6.economy: Build three cities to sustain the war effort.
m6.weather: Watch the sky: storms slow ships and aircraft down, and fog banks halve the range of radars.
m6.clock: The clock is ticking: the dial at the top announces the next milestone. A peace summit or a Council vote turns it back; bombs hasten it.
m6.push: Push towards forty percent. A vulnerable nation is marked on the map.

hint.research: Our research centres are idling: nothing is being studied. Open Technologies and pick a research, or queue several.

modeDesc.ffa: Free for all: the first to reach the land threshold wins.
modeDesc.teams: Players and nations are split into teams; a team's land adds up.
modeDesc.humansVsNations: All humans together, as one team, against the nations' coalition (they don't attack each other). Teammates can't attack each other: gifts of gold and troops, shared sight. The first side to reach the victory threshold wins.
modeDesc.tribes: No nations, only tribes. Ideal for practice.
modeDesc.doomsday: After 10 minutes a minimum share of land is required, and it keeps rising.
modeDesc.battleRoyale: Every 3 minutes a zone shrinks; land outside it becomes uninhabitable.
modeDesc.humansVsNationsSolo: You alone against a coalition of every nation: they never attack each other and may send each other reinforcements. Tribes belong to no side. The first side to reach the victory threshold wins; if you are eliminated, the coalition wins.

difficultyDesc.easy: Small armies; slow, cautious nations; few betrayals.
difficultyDesc.hard: Nations as strong as you, and more aggressive.
difficultyDesc.impossible: Bigger armies; fast and ruthless nations.

ruleDesc.allowPorts: Allows ports, warships and sea trade.
ruleDesc.allowNukes: Allows silos, A-bombs, H-bombs and MIRVs.
ruleDesc.allowDonations: Allows gifts of gold and troops between allies.
ruleDesc.waterNukes: Nuclear blasts over water also leave fallout.
ruleDesc.decontamination: Fallout disappears after 10 minutes instead of staying.
ruleDesc.allowSpectators: Allows spectators to join the game.
